hero.lead: Africa’s most populous nation, 237.5 million strong, whose 2025 Eurobond drew more than $13 billion of orders for $2.35 billion of paper.

capital.heading: Nigeria borrows at scale and the world bids for it. Next, a full table in every home.

record.text: Eurobonds, 10-year and 20-year: $1.25B at 8.625% to 2036 and $1.10B at 9.125% to 2046; orders above $13B
Nigeria Actions for Investment and Jobs Acceleration (NAIJA): Capital markets, power sector reform, trade and revenue
Sustainable Agricultural Value-Chains for Growth (AGROW): Up to one million farmers
Finance for small businesses: Credit for micro, small and medium enterprises

register.name: Eurobonds, 10-year and 20-year
register.note: $1.25B at 8.625% to 2036 and $1.10B at 9.125% to 2046; orders above $13B
register.text: The order book was more than five times the size of the issue: proof that capital will come when the case is clear.

register.name: Nigeria Actions for Investment and Jobs Acceleration (NAIJA)
register.note: Capital markets, power sector reform, trade and revenue
register.text: Supports reforms that deepen capital markets, speed electrification, lower trade barriers and widen access to good seed.

register.name: Sustainable Agricultural Value-Chains for Growth (AGROW)
register.text: Links smallholder farmers to agribusiness through matching grants, better seed and fertiliser systems and digital advice.

register.name: Finance for small businesses
register.note: Credit for micro, small and medium enterprises
register.text: Widens access to finance for the small firms that employ most Nigerians.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 64 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy open-air market street in Lagos, traders and shoppers seen at a distance

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Smallholder farms of cassava and maize in the green Middle Belt of Nigeria

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Dense tropical rainforest in Cross River State, Nigeria, morning mist in the canopy

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: The wide brown Niger River at its confluence with the Benue near Lokoja, Nigeria

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: Rows of solar panels of a village mini-grid in northern Nigeria under a bright sky

items.name: The enterprises building Perfect Nigeria
items.text: The Stewards are verifying the companies and social enterprises already delivering the seven basic living standards in Nigeria. Suggest one to include.

coverage.gap_text: Nigerians who cannot always count on enough good food: 76 in every hundred.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 76.5% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 28% cook with clean fuels and technology

guarantees.name: Education

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$4.20 a day; 64% live below it
